subject: physics_2
question_text: Magnetic lines form continuous closed loops. Why?

mark_split.label: The path of a field line

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: field lines run north to south outside a magnet and south to north inside it, closing every loop; the underlying reason is that isolated magnetic poles do not exist, so the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero (Gauss's law for magnetism) — the book gives only the path description; the no-monopole reason is added because the question asks why.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The path of a field line
lines: Outside a magnet, field lines run from the
north pole to the south pole. Inside the
magnet they continue from the south pole
back to the north pole. So every line
steps.margin_note: First mark. The inside part is what most answers miss — the line does not stop at the south pole.
steps.why: A field line seen only outside the magnet looks like it starts at N and ends at S. Following it through the magnet's inside shows it never ends — the outside and inside parts join into one loop.
common_mistakes: Saying lines start at the north pole and end at the south pole. They pass through the poles and continue inside the magnet.
Drawing the inside lines from north to south. Inside the magnet the direction is south to north.

recall.must_convey: That lines go north to south outside the magnet and south to north inside it, so each line closes into a loop.
accept: north to south outside, south to north inside
the line continues inside the magnet

steps.memory_tip: Follow one line all the way: out at N, around to S, and back through the body of the magnet to N.

steps.label: No monopoles
steps.mark_note: Flux through a closed surface is zero
lines: exist, so a field line cannot start or end
on a single pole, the way an electric line
starts and ends on charges. The net
magnetic flux through any closed surface
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The word why in the question asks for this reason — no monopoles, so no place for a line to start or end.
steps.why: Electric lines can end because isolated charges exist. No isolated magnetic pole has ever been found, so magnetic lines have nowhere to start or stop — closing into loops is the only possibility, and Gauss's law for magnetism states it as zero net flux.
common_mistakes: Answering only with the path description. The question asks why, and the reason is that monopoles do not exist.
Writing the flux as q/ε₀. That is the electric case — the magnetic flux through a closed surface is zero.

recall.must_convey: That isolated magnetic poles do not exist, so the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero.
accept: net flux through a closed surface is zero
reject: south to north inside the magnet

steps.memory_tip: Electric lines can end because lone charges exist; magnetic lines cannot because lone poles do not.

insider_note: This question is the 2-mark seed of the Gauss's law SAQ in this chapter — the phrase 'monopoles do not exist' earns in both places.
